I ran the conventions review (`--review-pr` mode) on `git diff 0bd81ad5...HEAD`: 2 commits, 10 files, all under `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/Policies/`. I went through every rule in `docs/engineering/sources/rules.json` and wrote the checklist to the scratchpad, not the repo. I changed no tracked files, ran no tests and didn't use `gh`. I didn't need to look up the review history behind any rule.

No rule is clearly broken. I found one medium issue against the written rules in `AGENTS.md`, and four low-severity ones against rules in `rules.json`.

## Findings

| # | Sev | Rule | File:line | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Medium | `AGENTS.md` → General Principles ("Comments are tech debt… keep it to one line… never multi-paragraph comment blocks") | `SpendingLimitIntroDialog/constants.ts:1`, `SpendingLimitIntroDialog/SpendingLimitPreview.tsx:7`, `:24`, `:57`, `SpendingLimitIntroDialog/index.tsx:10`, `:38`, `:44`, `Policies/index.tsx:25`, `:37`, `Policies.stories.tsx:25`, `SpendingLimitIntroDialog/SpendingLimitIntroDialog.stories.tsx:29` | These are 2–8 line comment blocks that explain design reasons or describe what the code does. Examples: "copy is verbatim from the design", why the key is browser-wide, how the cards "recede", and a story walkthrough. Cut each to one line with the non-obvious reason, or delete it. The one-line JSDoc on props (`index.tsx:32`, `:34`) is fine. |
| 2 | Low | TEST-02 (new branch logic needs branch-specific tests) | `Policies/index.tsx:44` / `__tests__/Policies.test.tsx:92` | The "proceed" path (`proceedToSpendingLimitFlow` → `closeSpendingLimitIntro` → `setHasSeenSpendingLimitIntro(true)`) has no page-level test. "records that it has been shown" only covers the Close button. If proceed stopped saving the flag, the intro would come back on every visit and no test would fail. Add a test that clicks "Set up spending limit" and expects `mockSetHasSeenSpendingLimitIntro` to be called with `true`. |
| 3 | Low | TEST-01 (assertions must fail on the regression they claim to cover) | `__tests__/Policies.test.tsx:101` | "does not explain again once it has been shown" only checks that the dialog is absent. It would still pass if the tile were disabled again (`isAvailable: false`) or `handleSelect` weren't wired. It doesn't prove the "already seen" branch ran. The flow behind it is an empty placeholder (`TODO(WA-3150)`), so there's nothing positive to assert yet. Either leave a note to add the assertion in WA-3150, or first check the tile is enabled and the click reached the handler. |
| 4 | Low | PROD-01 (product behavior changes need explicit confirmation) | `PolicyCatalogue/catalogue.ts:19` | The Spending limit tile is now shown as available, but `startSpendingLimitFlow` is empty (`Policies/index.tsx:16`). After the first dismissal, clicking the tile does nothing, with no feedback. The page is behind `FEATURES.POLICIES` (`pages/spaces/policies.tsx:14`), which limits the impact. Confirm with product that this is acceptable until WA-3150, or keep the flag off in production until then. |
| 5 | Low | UI-01 (use theme tokens) | `SpendingLimitIntroDialog/index.tsx:89` | `dark:text-black` uses a raw Tailwind colour instead of a theme token. It's also redundant: the default Button variant already sets `dark:[&_svg]:text-black` (`components/ui/button.tsx:37`), and that selector wins in dark mode anyway. Drop `dark:text-black` and the comment above it. |

## Rules that apply and pass
- **FEAT-01 / FEAT-03:** imports inside the feature are relative and cross-boundary imports go to `@/components/*`. No feature barrel imports itself.
- **UI-01:** `bg-[var(--color-background-light-hover)]` and `text-[var(--color-static-text-brand)]` follow patterns already used in `spaces` (e.g. `SpacesList/index.tsx:167`, `SpaceInfoModal/index.tsx:200`). The token logo is a hosted URL.
- **OBS-01:** tile-click tracking is still covered for both available (Proposer) and unavailable (Account recovery) tiles.
- **TEST-04:** the spending-limit assertions in `PolicyCatalogue.test.tsx` were moved to Account recovery, so the same behaviour is still tested.
- **TEST-05:** no MSW fixtures are imported into unit tests.
- **Sentence case (`AGENTS.md`):** all copy passes except "1,500/Month", which is design copy for an illustrative value.

The other rules (auth, RTK, chain, tx, mobile, CI, E2E, numbers, security) don't touch this diff.
